Bird watching is quiet at first, but the quiet part is actually what makes it interesting. A beginner usually notices color before anything else, then starts paying attention to wing shape, songs, and the way a bird moves through a tree. Early morning is the best time near the creek behind our school because sparrows, robins, and red-winged blackbirds all show up before the path gets busy. A small notebook helps more than an expensive camera because the notes catch behavior that a blurry picture misses.
